question.problem: Find the center and radius of the circle whose equation is ${x}^{2}+6x+{y}^{2}=40.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the center and radius of the circle, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+6x+{y}^{2} & =40 \\ ({x}^{2}+6x)+{y}^{2} & =40 \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot 3x+{3}^{2})+{y}^{2} & =40+{3}^{2} \\ ({x}^{2}+2\cdot 3x+{3}^{2})+{y}^{2} & =49\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can factor the perfect squares and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+3)^{2}+(y-0)^{2} & ={7}^{2} \\ (x-(-3))^{2}+(y-0)^{2} & ={7}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle is centered at $(-3,0)$ and its radius is $7.$
